column3: Direct continuation: followers seek to disown those who disowned them after punishment appears.
Calls for patience and prayer, but adds little to the rupture of followers and leaders.
Uses sabab as a means pursued, offering only lexical context for al-asbab.
Contrasts following falsehood with following truth, clarifying the moral weight of following.
Concerns those slain in God's way, not the severing of attachments at punishment.
Again uses sabab as a pursued means; only distant lexical support.
False associates fail their callers when punishment is seen, closely paralleling abandoned dependence.
Trials and patience do not specifically explain disavowal or severed ties.
Depicts something built remaining until hearts are cut apart, supporting the image of rupture.
At punishment, the weak and arrogant exchange blame and regret, paralleling follower-leader collapse.
Return to God amid calamity is not about the specific ties of 2:166.
Following behind in a commanded departure is unrelated to the judgment-scene following.
Defines worthy following by guidance and lack of demand, contrasting the misguided following in 2:166.
Guidance and mercy for the patient do not address the scene of disavowal.
Seeing the imminent threatened reality changes the faces of disbelievers, echoing seeing punishment.
Immediate context: rivals loved besides God and the wrongdoers see punishment and divine power.
The pilgrimage rite does not clarify the severing of followers from those followed.
Explicit bara'ah establishes the Qur'anic act of formal disavowal.
Those urging others to follow deny carrying their sins, directly illuminating failed responsibility between followers and leaders.
Concealment of guidance and curse only indirectly frames consequences of misleading others.
A destroyed people are seen fallen; punishment imagery without relational rupture.
Following inherited fathers despite a call toward punishment clarifies misguided following leading to ruin.
Repentance and clarification are not directly about disavowal or severed bonds.
The heart's truthful sight does not add to the judgmental seeing in 2:166.
A repeated journey by sabab gives only distant lexical context.
Cursing of persistent disbelievers supplies general consequence, not the followers' separation.
Seeing one's smallest evil deed gives broad accountability but no relational explanation.
Unexpected punishment is only a general parallel to punishment being seen.
Enduring punishment immediately develops the consequence introduced in 2:166.
Seeing neither sun nor cold in Paradise has no relevant relation.
Recognition of error after misguidance is a distant parallel to belated realization.
Divine oneness indirectly counters the rival attachments preceding 2:166.
Not cut off in Paradise contrasts lexically, but does not explain severed ties.
Cutting the road is unrelated to the bonds cut in 2:166.
Signs of God's ordering support divine power, not the particular relational collapse.
General lasting punishment of disbelievers adds little beyond the consequence.
Al-asbab are sought as access, offering lexical range but not the severance scene.
Punishment of disbelievers and unseen forces are only broadly related.
When enmity to God becomes clear, Abraham disowns his father; this explains disavowal after decisive knowledge.
Groups split their affair among themselves, directly supporting the image of ties breaking apart.
The signs given to Jesus do not clarify following, punishment, or severed bonds.
Following the Prophet is a positive following relation, but has no judgment rupture.
Deferred punishment becoming unavoidable only broadly echoes seeing punishment.
Receiving a sabab from God gives distant lexical context for al-asbab.
A sabab is extended then cut, strongly illustrating the wording of severed means while in another setting.
Commands following revelation rather than other protectors, directly contrasting the misplaced following behind 2:166.
God's full awareness on that day offers general judgment context only.
Commands faith and following the Messenger for guidance, contrasting the doomed relation of 2:166.
Conflict over the sleepers does not illuminate the followers and followed of 2:166.
Rain making earth green does not add to the focus ayah.
Senses fail to benefit deniers at consequence, a distant parallel to belated perception.
A commanded departure and an afflicted wife concern a different kind of separation.
Cutting the life-vein supplies vivid but nonrelational language for severance.
Seeing the greatest signs is not the seeing of punishment or broken allegiance.
Mutual disavowal of deeds clearly models separation of responsibility.
God's hearing and seeing gives no specific insight into the judgment scene.
Disowning the deeds of disobedient followers directly defines refusal of shared responsibility.
A second vision does not illuminate the punishment vision in 2:166.
Wrongdoers see punishment and seek a way back, closely matching the irreversible exposure of 2:166.
A contemptuous claim about who follows Noah only loosely relates to followers.
Following what angers God causes deeds to fail, explaining the fatal outcome of corrupt following.
Abraham's explicit disavowal of what his people worship shows principled separation from false allegiance.
The end of wrongdoers is general consequence without the relational pattern.
Following a rebellious devil identifies a paradigm of destructive following.
The disbelievers behold punishment at death, closely reinforcing the moment punishment is encountered.
Following revelation by a messenger is a positive model but does not address severance.
Mutual refusal to follow competing directions illustrates incompatible allegiances, though outside the punishment scene.
Affirms divine oneness and disavows association, countering the rival attachments behind 2:166.
Leaving outward and inward sin supplies only broad moral accountability.
A past punishment invites reflection but has no follower-followed relation.
Commands following the best revelation before sudden punishment, directly contrasting belated realization.
Breaking what God commanded to be joined and cutting it off gives a close conceptual counterpart to severed bonds.
At their Lord, weak and arrogant people trade accusations, closely expanding the collapse of dependent allegiance.
Refusal continues until painful punishment is seen, directly paralleling the timing of 2:166.
A fearful wartime vision does not provide the relational or judgment structure of the focus.
Signs do not avail until painful punishment is seen, directly reinforcing belated perception.
Following Jesus and final judgment are related only through the general term following.
Demanding to see God openly is unrelated to seeing punishment after false allegiance.
Following amid hardship is a positive, unrelated form of following.
Refusal to declare oneself innocent foregrounds personal responsibility, contrasting the disavowals in 2:166.
Satan abandons those he emboldened when the sides meet, a vivid parallel to a leader's disavowal of followers.
Breaking commanded ties and cutting what should be joined leads to curse and an evil abode, strongly clarifying severed bonds.
Shared punishment of wrongdoers removes the benefit of companionship, resonating with failed ties under punishment.
A messenger's warning that a people are ignorant adds only general context of impending punishment.
Following God's path and protection from punishment is a positive contrast only.
Following divine guidance avoids fear and grief, a broad contrast to wrong following.
Those in the Fire ask its keepers to call for relief, extending the post-punishment setting.
Deeds are seen and then disclosed on return to God, clarifying accountability exposed in the judgment scene.
Those seeking praise cannot escape punishment, supporting the exposure of false standing before punishment.
Following inherited fathers despite lack of guidance directly supplies the kind of misguided following at issue.
Turning toward an assigned direction has only distant language of sight and following.
Rejecting a setting star is not relevant to punishment or follower-leader severance.
Looking without sight is too general to clarify the focus ayah.
Seeing a proof in a temptation narrative does not add to 2:166.
Rules of modesty do not clarify the focus ayah.
Seeing crops yellow and then disbelieving is unrelated to broken allegiances.
Refusal of worship and final gathering are only general judgment context.
Creation and an appointed term provide general final-accountability context only.
Marital reconciliation and aversion do not illuminate 2:166.
Following a man alleged to be bewitched gives only a distant instance of misguided following.
At gathering, associates disown their worshippers after the parties are separated, closely matching 2:166.
The weak confront the arrogant leaders before God over having followed them, directly expanding 2:166.
Satan disowns responsibility after judgment, stressing that the misled bear their own response to his call.
Misleaders bear burdens alongside those whom they mislead, directly clarifying responsibility in following.
Those who associated partners identify them, and the partners reject their claim, closely paralleling disavowal.
The wrongdoer regrets taking a person as an intimate companion, illuminating fatal human attachment.
The intimate companion leads one away from remembrance, directly explaining a destructive following bond.
A companion's misleading is exposed after remembrance had come, extending the regret of false attachment.
In the Fire, people say they obeyed their masters and great ones, directly naming the follower-leader relation.
The followers say their masters and great ones led them astray, directly supplying the accusation implicit in 2:166.
The followers ask doubled punishment and curse for those leaders, completing the post-punishment reversal.
The arrogant deny having turned the weak from guidance, directly continuing the leader-follower dispute of 34:31-33.
The followers turn to question one another, opening a scene of accountability among the condemned.
Followers accuse those addressed of approaching them from the right, directly portraying misleading influence.
Those addressed deny belief in the followers, separating influence from the followers' own refusal.
The accused leaders deny authority over the followers, directly clarifying divided responsibility.
The word of punishment becomes due upon both parties, directly matching their shared exposure to punishment.
Misleaders admit leading others astray because they themselves were astray, directly explaining the chain of following.
All become sharers in punishment, a direct counterpart to the collapse of their former relation.
In the Fire, the weak dispute with the arrogant, directly restating the hierarchy exposed by punishment.
Close friends become enemies on that day except the reverent, strongly clarifying severed human bonds.
Satan induces disbelief and then declares himself free of the person, a close pattern of disavowal after ruin.
Abraham and those with him declare disavowal and lasting enmity toward their people's worship, defining bara'ah.
Taking rabbis and monks as lords besides God directly supplies a form of misplaced allegiance to the followed.
Forbids taking fathers and brothers as protectors when they prefer disbelief, sharpening the limits of kin allegiance.
Worldly loves are weighed against God and His cause, directly contextualizing attachments that fail at judgment.
Whoever takes Satan as an ally is led astray and guided to the punishment of the Blaze.
Those who divide their religion into factions are disowned by the Messenger, combining fragmentation and disavowal.
Forbids following Satan's steps, giving the broader warning against destructive following.
Satan commands indecency and false speech about God, specifying the direction of that following.
Again forbids following Satan's steps, a broad warning relevant to misplaced following.
Forbids obeying disbelievers because they turn believers back as losers, directly addressing harmful obedience.
Forbids following desires of people who went astray and led many astray, a clear general analogue.
Following conjecture and guesswork turns one from God's path, framing a false basis for following.
Commands following God's straight path rather than diverging paths, a positive contrast to 2:166.
A person follows desire after abandoning God's signs and becomes a target of Satan, illustrating corrupt following.
Following desire after rejecting signs is contrasted with guidance, reinforcing responsibility for the chosen path.
Most people follow only conjecture, identifying an unreliable basis for collective following.
Forbids inclining toward wrongdoers, supplying a warning against attachment to those facing the Fire.
Satan's authority is over those who take him as ally and associate others, explaining a destructive allegiance.
Each people are called with their leader, adding judgment-day accountability through collective leadership.
In distress at sea, those called besides God vanish from memory, exposing the fragility of rival reliance.
Those who take God's servants as protectors face a false expectation, paralleling misplaced dependence.
Later generations neglect prayer and follow desires, a general pattern of ruin through following.
Following divine guidance prevents loss and misery, providing the positive counterpoint to 2:166.
Even parental pressure toward association must not be obeyed, limiting loyalty to close human ties.
Parents urging association are not to be obeyed, directly distinguishing companionship from obedience.
God forbids worshipping Satan because he is an open enemy, clarifying the danger of satanic allegiance.
Satan has led many astray, a concise account of mass misleading.
Disbelievers ask to see those who led them astray so they may abase them, extending post-judgment blame.
One who turns from remembrance receives a devil as a close companion, explaining a binding false attachment.
Such companions turn people from the path while they think themselves guided, directly illuminating deception in following.
Those invoked besides God cannot answer and are unaware of their callers, showing failed dependence.
A people follow those whose wealth and children only increase loss, a concise example of ruinous following.
